outcome.en: Replace a recipient with an indirect pronoun in a short shop conversation.
outcome.it: Sostituisci il destinatario con un pronome indiretto in un breve dialogo in negozio.

outcome.en: Compare two things, two qualities or equal characteristics.
outcome.it: Confronta due cose, due qualità o caratteristiche uguali.

outcome.en: Describe repeated past routines and the way things used to be.
outcome.it: Descrivi abitudini passate e com’erano le cose.

outcome.en: Use the present conditional for a request, a wish and a suggestion.
outcome.it: Usa il condizionale presente per una richiesta, un desiderio e un consiglio.

outcome.en: Say whether anyone is available and whether you can manage a task.
outcome.it: Di’ se qualcuno è disponibile e se riesci a svolgere un compito.

outcome.en: Use stare + gerund to describe an action in progress.
outcome.it: Usa stare + gerundio per descrivere un’azione in corso.

outcome.en: Use direct pronouns with the passato prossimo and with an infinitive.
outcome.it: Usa i pronomi diretti con il passato prossimo e con un infinito.

outcome.en: Identify a person or place using one clear relative clause.
outcome.it: Identifica una persona o un luogo con una proposizione relativa chiara.

outcome.en: Combine past background with completed events in an original travel story.
outcome.it: Combina lo sfondo passato con eventi conclusi in un racconto di viaggio originale.

outcome.en: Distinguish time required in general from the time a person takes.
outcome.it: Distingui il tempo necessario in generale dal tempo impiegato da una persona.

outcome.en: Use affirmative and negative tu instructions, including a single pronoun.
outcome.it: Usa istruzioni affermative e negative con tu, anche con un pronome.

outcome.en: Use servire and quello che to explain a practical need.
outcome.it: Usa servire e quello che per spiegare una necessità pratica.

outcome.en: Use formal Lei instructions with affirmative, negative and pronoun forms.
outcome.it: Usa istruzioni con il Lei formale, nelle forme affermative, negative e con pronomi.

outcome.en: Distinguish describing a good thing from doing something well.
outcome.it: Distingui la descrizione di una cosa buona dal fare bene qualcosa.

outcome.en: Use the simple future for plans and a clearly labelled guess about now.
outcome.it: Usa il futuro semplice per progetti e una supposizione esplicita sul presente.

outcome.en: Link a possible condition to a practical plan and use andarsene as a fixed expression.
outcome.it: Collega una condizione possibile a un progetto pratico e usa andarsene come espressione fissa.

outcome.en: Contrast an action in progress with one about to begin and link a short story.
outcome.it: Distingui un’azione in corso da una che sta per iniziare e collega un breve racconto.

outcome.en: Use past modal verbs with a stated auxiliary model and clear reflexive placement.
outcome.it: Usa i verbi modali al passato con un modello di ausiliare indicato e una posizione riflessiva chiara.

outcome.en: Recognise and form a small set of present subjunctives in housing sentences.
outcome.it: Riconosci e forma un piccolo gruppo di congiuntivi presenti in frasi sulla casa.

outcome.en: Choose between a taught che + subjunctive frame and secondo me + indicative.
outcome.it: Scegli fra un modello studiato con che + congiuntivo e secondo me + indicativo.

unitSourceMapping.outcome: Replace an already named destination with ci; distinguish location from the thing being discussed.
Retain a stated quantity while replacing the named item with ne; distinguish part of a set from a whole object.
Describe general activities and singular/plural things sold or used, without naming the person acting.
Distinguish very high degree from the highest/lowest degree within a stated group.
Form common -mente adverbs and distinguish describing a person or thing from describing an action.
Write contracted compound numbers, required -tré accents, dates and agreed ordinal labels.
Recognise letter-pattern and written-stress information; practise spelling without claiming automatic speech assessment.

programme.freshPractice: Each day requires its own saved learner output and self-checked criteria, even when linked lessons were completed earlier. Output is self-assessed, not automatically graded.
programme.budget: Five-minute personal checkpoint; linked grammar and missions can take multiple sittings within the learner’s selected daily budget. No calendar-duration guarantee.
programme.prerequisites: Prerequisite closures allocated in topological order, at most two newly introduced units per day. All original28 plus seven new A1 units are introduced by the end of Plus1; all20 A2 units by the end of Plus2. Revision days reuse previously introduced targets.
programme.diagnosticScope: The A1 readiness check retains its12 existing foundation domains. It does not comprehensively assess all32 A1 units or the20 A2 units; unit practice and self-assessed chapter responses are separate evidence.

limits: A1 readiness and tense diagnostics retain their A1 scope; new A2 lesson completion does not imply an A2 assessment result.
The present subjunctive is an introductory final-chapter extension, not general subjunctive mastery.
Optional existing A1 resources support prerequisite refreshes in A2 enrichment.
Source worksheets, solutions and independent homework are not reproduced; learner tasks and models are original.
All accessible main-book pages are captured privately; pedagogical review and original task coverage remain selective.
Plus2 publisher extent264 differs from the263 accessible reader pages; no missing page content or blank page is inferred.

validation.sourceMetadata: Five newly catalogued PDF records verified: three publisher support PDFs and two derived reader exports. Actual derived-PDF hashes, complete-book extraction hashes, final manifests and physical page extents agree.
independentReviewCorrections: Aligned every requested dialogue turn count with its model and preserved the buyer/helper speaker roles.
Added the Plus 2 contents citation for locative ci rather than attributing it only to imperfect-guide pages.
Used idiomatic fai una pausa and kept the Italian recall question entirely in Italian.
Kept the Plus 1 production examples within their intended chapter grammar; the family model distinguishes one relative from a plural group.
validation.nativeSourceChecksums: Both actual derived-PDF file hashes match their final manifests and page-preserving complete-book extracts.
validation.nativeSectionOffsets: Each book’s26 section ranges partition its actual physical pages exactly, without gaps or padding.
validation.nativeBookReview: Relevant main-book chapter content and complete grammar-reference text reviewed; source facts remain distinct from original portal explanations.

remainingLearningGaps.topic: Detailed plural-spelling families and further irregular nouns
remainingLearningGaps.status: Added original spelling-pattern practice with explicit exceptions and the six specified feminine body-plural models. The lessons teach bounded learned forms, not an exhaustive prediction of every Italian plural.

remainingLearningGaps.topic: A2 nonlocative ci and noun alterations
remainingLearningGaps.status: Added pensare a → ci with finite/modal placement and transparent literal -ino/-ina/-one/-ona formations. Other senses of ci, lexicalised alterations and affective/register differences remain outside these small units.

remainingLearningGaps.topic: Auxiliary alternation with cominciare/finire and ne with past-participle agreement
remainingLearningGaps.status: Added actor/task versus event constructions with cominciare/finire and partitive ne agreement for explicit countable quantities, including one item. Other alternating verbs and broader ne agreement contexts remain separate topics.

Added regular/irregular voi commands with both declared negative-pronoun positions, all five short tu-command families with the gli exception, and the pre-noun bello paradigm contrasted with ordinary post-noun agreement. Longer clitic combinations remain outside the bounded unit.

remainingLearningGaps.topic: Formal writing, causal connectors and further chapter vocabulary
remainingLearningGaps.status: Added invariant bisogna + infinitive, common perché/siccome cause ordering, consequence contrast and one original formal enquiry with coherent Lei/La/Le. Complete employment documents, CV composition and exhaustive chapter vocabulary remain partial.
Written recognition, original speaking prompts and self-checks are provided. Archiving media does not establish listening comprehension, transcription accuracy or automatically scored pronunciation.

gapContentEnhancement.preservation: All prior55 units,56 missions,56 enrichments, banks and four programme/day arrays retain their exact objects and order.
gapContentEnhancement.assessmentLimit: Practice and self-checks extend the bounded topics; no full-book teaching-completeness, CEFR certification or automatic pronunciation assessment is claimed.
